points.description: A static array lives/persists for the whole life of the program (retains its values between function calls), unlike a non-static (local) array.
points.partial_credit: Half or more if the persistence/lifetime idea is stated vaguely or only partly (e.g. only 'keeps its values' or only 'lasts longer') or with a minor error.

points.description: A static array is initialized only once, when the function declaring it is first called (a non-static array is re-created/re-initialized on every call).
points.partial_credit: Half if it says initialized once without saying when, or only that non-static is re-initialized each call.

rubric.notes: Full marks need the core fact: a static array lasts for the whole program run (keeps its values between calls), in any wording. Give part marks for vague or half-stated lifetime ideas, and for the 'initialized once at first call' detail alone, which earns P2 only. Give no marks for answers about unrelated things such as array size, or for wrong claims, like saying static arrays are destroyed when the function ends.
